newsitem.title: USA: Minnesotans argue over campaign against "squaw" names.
newsitem.headline: Minnesotans argue over campaign against "squaw" names.

text.p: Some American Indians are pushing to get the word "squaw" removed from dozens of streams, lakes and other geographic features across Minnesota, saying the word is offensive.
But other Minnesotans say they're offended by the campaign.
"Squaw" offends some Indians, who say it's a French corruption of an Iroqoui epithet for vagina.

Although some people in the Gopher State dispute that linguistic theory, the state legislature recently ordered that 19 place names inside lands under state control be changed, according to a Minnesota Department of Natural Resources.
As a result, Squaw Point is now Oak Point. The former Squaw Creek became Fond-du-lac Creek. And two lakes named Squaw were renamed -- one Wahbegon Lake, the other Equay Lake.
Residents of the town of Squaw Lake, near a body of water that once shared the same name, are resisting what they see as an attack on tradition by the forces of political correctness.

"Most people around here don't want it changed," lifelong Squaw Lake resident Sandra Strief said in a telephone interview Tuesday. "It doesn't mean to us what they say it means. When they say 'Squaw Lake', I just think of an Indian lady. I don't think of anything bad."
